paper_metadata.title: Quantum Optimization for Network Capacity Expansion of Microgrid Models via Grover-Enhanced QAOA

summary: The paper studies a Grover-enhanced QAOA for an 11-binary-variable microgrid network expansion problem derived from a PyPSA model. Using noiseless statevector simulation and 5000-shot sampling, the exact classical optimum 11110111011 with objective value -5 appears with probability 0.0166 at 1 layer, is not among the top-5 at 2 layers, reaches 0.1730 at 3 layers, and drops to 0.1172 at 4 layers, while the best empirical outcome at 4 layers is 0.2090.

experiments.description: Grover-enhanced QAOA applied to an 11-binary-variable microgrid network expansion instance derived from a PyPSA model, evaluated at QAOA depths 1 through 4 using noiseless statevector simulation and 5000-shot sampling; compared against a classical Gurobi optimum.

hyperparameters.beta: integer number of Grover iterations per layer

algorithm.parameter_initialization: coarse grid search over discrete beta-vectors, then refine gamma with L-BFGS-B; initial state is uniform superposition H^⊗n|0⟩^⊗n

optimizer_settings.parameter_bounds: gamma in (0, pi]; beta as nonnegative integers

problem_formulation.encoding_details: 1 qubit per binary decision variable; 11 binary variables encode modular generator capacity, line capacity increments, conductor selectors, and load-connection decisions
problem_formulation.objective_function: Minimize G0,B0 + 2G1,B0 - (5/2) * sum_{k=0}^{2} s_Bk + 6 z_L0-1 + 1 z_L1-2 (as written in the paper; cost vector also given as c=[1,2,0,0,6,0,0,1,-5,-5,-5])
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Hard feasibility enforced by Grover oracle marking exactly classically feasible states; soft penalty term lambda*max(0, tau - m_F) added during parameter search
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: Diagonal cost Hamiltonian on 11 qubits; implementation uses H_impl = 15 I + sum_i a_i Z_i with a=[1,2,0,0,6,0,0,1,-5,-5,-5]

problem_instance.description: Small representative distribution-network microgrid expansion instance from a PyPSA model with 3 buses and candidate generators/lines

dataset_specification.description: 3-bus network (B0, B1, B2) with candidate generators, branches L0-1 and L1-2, and local loads

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Classical MILP solved with Gurobi to obtain reference optimum and enumerate feasible binary assignments; no ML-style preprocessing reported
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Noiseless statevector simulation plus 5000-shot sampling; results reported for QAOA depths 1, 2, 3, and 4; compared to Gurobi global optimum

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: PyPSA model converted to MILP; feasible assignments enumerated classically; cost Hamiltonian constructed from linear coefficients
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Statevector probabilities converted to expected cost and empirical frequencies from 5000 samples; best observed candidates and exact optimum probability reported

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: non-monotonic across depth; exact optimum probability reported for p=1,2,3,4

speedup_claims.caveats: The paper presents a proof-of-concept simulation and does not claim asymptotic or empirical speedup over the classical Gurobi solver.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: No hardware execution; 11-qubit noiseless statevector simulation with 5000-shot sampling and a classical Gurobi baseline.
limiting_factors: No demonstrated quantum speedup over Gurobi
Only noiseless simulation, not QPU execution
Optimization uses a mixed discrete-continuous grid+refine search that is not shown to scale
Classical baseline remains the reference optimum

notes: hardware.type reported as noiseless statevector simulator (Qiskit Aer AerSimulator with method='statevector')
num_qubits inferred from the paper's 11 binary variables and explicit statement that the instance is an 11-qubit design instance
